work.abstract_text: Using Brimkov's earlier starlike enumeration (May 2017, Proposition 7.11), we answer Mukherjee and Ray's Problem 5.3 in On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees, arXiv:2611.10985v1 (2026), Section 5, p. 21, negatively even for two three-leaf trees and even when their order may be exchanged. For every n at least 10 we construct such a pair: its coefficient differences at sizes 4, 6, n-2 are -2, 1, -1, so neither order admits the requested single crossing. The construction follows from an explicit enumeration of connected forcing sets in a three-armed tree. We also explain the smaller, ordered path-star obstruction from the posers' own examples. For the neighboring unicyclic problem, a complete five-vertex classification shows that a fixed-leaf class can have neither a least nor a greatest polynomial.

work.title: Three-leaf counterexamples to Mukherjee and Ray's connected-forcing crossing question
